OK I blogged it.

natesilver.net/p/nuclear-bri…
I guess I'll have to blog about this tomorrow, but "LOL, Trump TACO'ed out" is decidedly not the right reaction as compared to "that kind of brinkmanship is really fucking dangerous".
Man that Michigan team was really good. In fact, they finished with our 3rd-highest year-end COOPER rating ever. Congrats to the Wolverines and the Big Ten!

More here, plus video of my chat this afternoon with @galendruke.

natesilver.net/p/iran-is-tru…
But Trump's decision to go to war with Iran has to be in the highest category of political blunders.
It's become common for presidents to overread their mandates. I don't think there's enough adjustment for how much narrower and more contingent victory margins are than they used to be.

12pm on the Not Everything App that is 8 letters long and begins with an 'S'.

We might talk a little bit of Twitter stuff at the top, too.


Galen Druke (@galendruke)

Trump praising Allah on Easter?! Threatening to bomb Iranian civilian infrastructure by Tuesday?!

Come join @NateSilver538 and me for a chat about the political fallout of all of it all at 12pm Eastern today!





— https://nitter.net/galendruke/status/2041166952475808171#m

In what sense is it intellectually dishonest, Nikita? The context is clear. My thesis is: I think your algo surfaces too little quality. And I think your excuses in these back-and-forth exchanges have been validating of that. To your credit, it's clear enough you agree with me.


Nikita Bier (@nikitabier)

Can you stop quote tweeting without the context? It’s intellectually dishonest.



— https://nitter.net/nikitabier/status/2041011662820634839#m

There's nothing organic about it; it's deliberate choices you and the team are making. And although those choices may have been defensible in the abstract, they're clearly resulting in low-quality content rising to the top. You're a smart dude, you can build a better algo!


Nikita Bier (@nikitabier)

It’s paywalled. 

If only 0.1% of users can derive value from the content, it will organically rank lower.



— https://nitter.net/nikitabier/status/2041009771235692983#m

Honestly seems woke to be this relativistic? Hopefully we can walk and chew gum at the same time and recognize 1) this was a dumb typo, 2) sometimes NYT/MSM make more serious fuckups, and 3) Catturd shouldn't get 50x the engagement of serious reporting on endangered soldiers.


Stephen L. Miller (@redsteeze)

New York Times couldn't get the initials for NATO right three days ago. 

"Twitter needs to be artificially boosting the New York Times more" 

The amount of digging on this here it's kind

It can't be *that* hard to create a version of Twitter/X that removes some of the groupthink but still promotes high-quality engagement and content. And is a portal to the rest of the internet rather than a closed ecosystem, always one of the good things about pre-Elon Twitter.

Yeah that sucked and was bad.

If you check out my history, you'll know I'm not afraid to criticize the mainstream media. I also had a lot of bad experiences on Twitter circa 2018-2021.

It should be a low bar to clear. I don't think the current iteration of X is clearing it.


EducatëdHillbilly™ (@RobProvince)

Old twitter banned me after I DM’d the Hunter Biden laptop story. 

Eat me Nate.



— https://nitter.net/RobProvince/status/2040977101071778107#m

A (super cute!!) pet photo from Catturd™ gets literally 50x the engagement of a link to incredibly important original reporting from the NYT on Iran. According to your own on-site numbers @nikitabier. Do you consider this to be a desirable outcome?

It seems e.g. like lots of people clicking on a link would be an unambiguous signal of engagement. It's *off-platform* engagement, and you guys have the right to deprioritize that. But that's what Facebook did, and it made them literally completely irrelevant to the news convo.

That isn't really what the tweet you're self-quoting says. It says it's hard to establish the quality signal associated with a link and so each tweet should "stand alone", and also the platform design makes it hard to engage with such tweets. Maybe fix that?




Nikita Bier (@nikitabier)

Links are not deboosted. We fixed that issue last year.



— https://nitter.net/nikitabier/status/2040968250604102105#m

The NYT published a link to critical original reporting on Iran 45 minutes ago. A good, fair story. They have 53m followers.  The engagement metrics you display say they got 94 likes and 33 retweets out of that. Is that accurate? And if so, shouldn't you work on a better algo?

Do you think that X is facilitating high-quality information? If you suppress external links and there's no real quality signal other than engagement, and people aren't even getting so the accounts they follow so much as the algo, it seems like this is about where you'd end up.

It's not my data.

The source is Cluvio, which is linked to in the article. I'd link to it in this tweet, but ironically, that would kill engagement.

And I know that traffic is hard to count. Especially for a private company. But if you have more accurate data, then publish it.


Nikita Bier (@nikitabier)

Data isn’t accurate. Missing half the network.





— https://nitter.net/nikitabier/status/2040956972338754027#m

Longer analysis here, with some context about the last decade or so in the media business.
